Why can't you detect endianness with int v= 1,

Endianness is the order in which the bytes of a multi-byte value are stored in memory or sent over a link. A CPU register has no endianness; it only appears when a value is split into bytes at an address, on a wire, or in a file.
least significant byte at the lowest address.

ARM is bi-endian by architecture but nearly always runs little-endian, including Cortex-M and Linux on SoCs like Aspeed BMC parts. Check the TRM for Cortex-R and legacy designs. x86 and RISC-V are little-endian. Classic PowerPC, SPARC and some MIPS and network processors are big-endian.
Network byte order (TCP/IP) is big-endian, hence
. They are no-ops on a big-endian host.

I2C defines no byte order; the device datasheet decides. Many sensors send MSB first (big-endian), while SMBus word transfers send the low byte first (little-endian). This mismatch is a classic bug source.

Each protocol picks its own order. USB and PCIe are generally little-endian, PLDM multi-byte fields are little-endian per the DMTF specs, and CAN signals can be Intel (little) or Motorola (big) per the DBC file. Always check the field definitions in the spec.

Parse with shifts. Shifts act on values, so the code is correct on any host.
Avoid bitfields for wire formats and register maps: bitfield ordering within a word is implementation-defined. Use masks and shifts.

A heap-allocated stack has no guard page: if the task uses more than you gave it, it silently overwrites the next heap block. See stack overflow detection below.
A new task has never run, so nothing was ever saved for it. We

it was interrupted just before its first instruction: we build, by hand, the same frame the hardware and the PendSV handler would have pushed. The first context switch to the task then "returns" into its entry function.

uint32_t *build_initial_frame(uint32_t *sp, void (*entry)(void *), void *arg)
{
  *--sp = 0x01000000u;                              /* xPSR: Thumb bit (T) set */
  *--sp = ((uint32_t)entry) & 0xFFFFFFFEu;          /* PC  : task entry        */
  *--sp = (uint32_t)task_exit;                      /* LR  : if entry returns  */
  *--sp = 0;                                        /* R12 */
  *--sp = 0; *--sp = 0; *--sp = 0;                  /* R3, R2, R1 */
  *--sp = (uint32_t)arg;                            /* R0  : first argument    */
  for (int r = 11; r >= 4; r--) { *--sp = 0; }      /* R11..R4 (software part) */
  return sp;                                        /* saved into tcb->sp */
}
R4 R5 R6 R7 R8 R9 R10 R11

PendSV_Handler:
    mrs   r0, psp
    stmdb r0!, {r4-r11}         @ save R4-R11 below the hardware frame
    ldr   r1, =current_tcb
    ldr   r2, [r1]
    str   r0, [r2]              @ current->sp = psp
    push  {r1, lr}              @ keep r1 and EXC_RETURN across the call
    bl    sched_pick_next       @ returns the next tcb in r0
    pop   {r1, lr}
    str   r0, [r1]              @ current_tcb = next
    ldr   r0, [r0]              @ r0 = next->sp
    ldmia r0!, {r4-r11}         @ restore R4-R11
    msr   psp, r0
    bx    lr                    @ EXC_RETURN 0xFFFFFFFD: thread mode, use PSP
